question: Should OpenClaw publish a supported OpenAPI/Swagger contract for Gateway programmatic access, and should that contract cover HTTP endpoints only, Gateway WebSocket/RPC schemas, or the public SDK path?
rationale: The implementation choice would become a public API, auth, versioning, and client-generation contract across stable Gateway surfaces, so automation should not choose the boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Keep Open For API Direction
options.body: Use this issue to decide the supported schema scope, auth disclosure, versioning, and drift checks before adding a generated artifact or runtime route.

options.title: Scope To HTTP OpenAPI
options.body: Sponsor a narrow PR for selected Gateway HTTP endpoints with generated spec, docs, auth warnings, and drift tests.

options.title: Fold Into SDK Track
options.body: Redirect this only if maintainers decide the public SDK/WebSocket client track is the sole supported custom-client path and preserve the client-generation need there.

recommendation.title: Keep Open For API Direction
recommendation.body: Use this issue to decide the supported schema scope, auth disclosure, versioning, and drift checks before adding a generated artifact or runtime route.
